stem: Polonium-211 (²¹¹₈₄Po) decays by alpha emission to form a stable isotope of lead (Pb).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for this decay.

²¹¹₈₄Po → ⁽[[blank]]⁾₍[[blank]]₎Pb + ⁽[[blank]]⁾₍[[blank]]₎α

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
The variation with time *t* of the number of unstable nuclei *N* in a sample of polonium-211 is shown in Fig. 9.1.

[[fig:f1]]

At time *t* = 0, the sample contains only polonium-211.
parts.text: Use Fig. 9.1 to determine the decay constant λ of polonium-211. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(i) to calculate the activity at time *t* = 0 of the sample of polonium-211.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 9.1, sketch a line to show the variation with *t* of the number of lead nuclei in the sample.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Each decay releases an alpha particle with energy 690 keV.
parts.text: Calculate, in J, the total amount of energy given to alpha particles that are emitted between time *t* = 0.30 s and time *t* = 0.90 s.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why the total amount of energy released by the decay process between time *t* = 0.30 s and time *t* = 0.90 s is greater than your answer in (c)(i).

figures.caption: Fig. 9.1
figures.alt: A graph of the number of unstable nuclei N, in units of 10¹², against time t in seconds, showing a decreasing curved line.
